mainEntity.name: What should I do if my porcelain veneer falls off?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a veneer becomes fully detached, keep it safe and contact your dental practice to arrange an appointment as soon as conveniently possible. Avoid attempting to reattach the veneer yourself using household adhesives, as these are not appropriate for dental use and could damage the tooth surface or create difficulties for your dentist when reattaching or replacing the veneer. In most cases, a detached veneer is not a dental emergency, but prompt assessment is advisable to protect the exposed tooth.

mainEntity.name: Can a loose veneer be re-bonded?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, a veneer that has become detached can be re-bonded by your dentist, provided the veneer itself remains intact and the underlying tooth structure is in good condition. Your dentist will clean the surfaces, assess the bond, and re-cement the veneer using an appropriate dental adhesive. However, if the tooth has developed decay or the veneer has fractured, a replacement may be necessary. Individual clinical assessment is needed to determine the most appropriate course of action.

mainEntity.name: Does teeth grinding damage porcelain veneers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bruxism — grinding or clenching the teeth — can place significant stress on porcelain veneers and the adhesive bond securing them. Over time, this may contribute to veneer loosening, chipping, or fracture. Patients with bruxism are often advised to wear a custom-made night guard to help protect their dental restorations during sleep. If you are concerned that you may be grinding your teeth, it is worth raising this with your dental team so that appropriate protective measures can be discussed.

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if my veneer is starting to fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs that a veneer may be failing include increased tooth sensitivity — particularly to cold — a sensation of movement or rocking when biting, visible discolouration along the edges of the veneer, or a noticeable gap between the veneer and the tooth. In some cases, patients may experience mild discomfort when eating. If you notice any of these signs, it is advisable to arrange a dental appointment. Early assessment often allows for simpler and less costly intervention than waiting until a problem becomes more advanced.

mainEntity.name: Do porcelain veneers require special cleaning products?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain veneers can generally be maintained with a standard oral hygiene routine — brushing twice daily with a fluoride toothpaste and cleaning between teeth with floss or interdental brushes. It is advisable to use a non-abrasive toothpaste, as highly abrasive whitening products may gradually affect the surface finish of the veneer. Alcohol-based mouthwashes used in excess may also affect the bonding agent over time. Your dentist or dental hygienist can recommend the most suitable products based on your individual oral health needs.

mainEntity.name: How often should I have my veneers checked?

acceptedAnswer.text: Veneers should be included as part of your routine dental examinations. The frequency of check-ups your dentist recommends will depend on your overall oral health, but attending at least once or twice per year is common guidance for most patients. Regular examinations allow your dentist to assess the condition of the veneers, check for any early signs of wear or bond failure, and monitor the health of the surrounding gum tissue and underlying teeth. Consistent professional care is one of the most effective ways to support the longevity of dental restorations.
